exercise.name: Front Plank with Arm and Leg Lift
aliases: Forearm plank with opposite arm and leg raise

reference.title: Front Plank with Arm and Leg Lift (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

exercise.mechanics: Isometric trunk (anti-extension, anti-rotation) with shoulder flexion and hip extension

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the arm and leg lift, breathe in as they return; keep the brace on.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s out, 1 s hold, 1 s back per side

prescription.tempo: 1 s out, 1 s hold, 1 s back
prescription.progression: Longer holds, then slower reps; regress to the bird dog on all fours

cues.text: Forearm plank: elbows under the shoulders, feet hip width or a little wider for balance.
Shift the weight a touch onto the left forearm, then reach the right arm forward and lift the left leg; hips stay level.
Hold briefly: long line from the fingertips to the lifted heel, no twisting.
Return the forearm and the toes to the mat under control.
Other side: left arm forward, right leg up, hold, return.

mistakes.mistake: Hips twisting toward the lifted leg
mistakes.fix: Keep both hip bones facing the mat; lift less if needed.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching as the leg lifts
mistakes.fix: Lift from the glute, only as high as the pelvis stays level.

mistakes.mistake: Shoulder of the support arm sinking
mistakes.fix: Push the mat away with the supporting forearm.
Widen the feet a little for a stable base.

kinematics.norm: Reaching arm forward, about level with the shoulder (clinical opinion)
A small lift past the body line keeps the pelvis level (clinical opinion); hip extension in a plank raised gluteal activity (Boren 2011)
Held straight on the two support points (clinical opinion)
Level and square; contralateral lifts load the obliques as anti-rotators (clinical opinion; Ekstrom 2007 for the quadruped arm and leg lift)
About 1 s out, 1 s hold, 1 s back (clinical opinion)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low back pain that increases in the plank: shorten the hold or drop to the knee plank.
High blood pressure: breathe steadily; long breath-held efforts raise blood pressure.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: hands together (forearms in a slight V) or an incline plank with the forearms on a bench.
Elbow discomfort: fold the mat under the forearms.

muscleNotes.core: The two-point base asks the abdominals to resist both sagging and rotation (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Obliques resist the rotation created by lifting opposite limbs (clinical opinion; Ekstrom 2007 measured high oblique activity in the quadruped arm and leg lift).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Obliques resist the rotation created by lifting opposite limbs (clinical opinion; Ekstrom 2007 measured high oblique activity in the quadruped arm and leg lift).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Gluteus maximus extends the lifted leg; hip extension from a plank gave high gluteal activity in Boren 2011.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Gluteus maximus extends the lifted leg; hip extension from a plank gave high gluteal activity in Boren 2011.
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Anterior deltoid holds the reaching arm forward (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Anterior deltoid holds the reaching arm forward (clinical opinion).
